# Re-measure ring timing for one-level hex deployments (AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A)

Discovered-from: AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2 (In HexMap killing the mini-boss wins the hex).

## Problem statement

The measured ring baseline (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, GDD §8.2
"Measured ring timings") models a deployment as the **classic campaign slice**
from the hex's aggression-selected level through to the campaign's final boss.
The mini-boss ending turns a deployment into exactly **one** campaign level,
ending on that level's wave-10 mini-boss, so the per-deployment duration, the
per-ring deployment count and every derived ring window move — and the
committed evidence no longer measures the game a player plays.

## Users

- **As a Hangar War player**, I want the ring budgets to describe sorties I
  actually fly — one hex, one level, one mini-boss — so the advertised
  "40–60 minute ring" is the time I will really spend.
- **As a producer**, I want the timing evidence regenerated from the shipped
  one-level deployment, so a pacing ruling rests on measured numbers rather
  than on a model of a campaign slice that no longer exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `createArenaDeploymentRunner` plays the **shipped one-level deployment**
  (the hex's aggression-selected level, through the arena's per-level mode)
  and derives each deployment's duration from the arena's `level_cleared`
  transition: a cleared level is a **captured** deployment, a player death
  before it is a **loss**. `npm run ring-timing -- --json --out
  docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` regenerates the artifact on the shipped
  code with no hand-edited numbers.
- The retry allowance charges the **replayed deployment's own measured
  length** instead of the fixed 5-minute window, and the between-sortie
  allowance stays at the documented **2 minutes**; both are stated in the
  harness documentation and pinned by a test. A rush-line re-capture is charged
  the line's **measured mean deployment + the same 2-minute visit**, replacing
  the retired 18 000-tick window (producer ruling Q4 = a).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 (the measured table, the supported
  playstyles numbers and the "a deployment is" sentence) and the docs guards
  (`src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`, `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`)
  match the regenerated artifact. Any ring whose budget no longer holds is
  recorded with its new measurement **and opened as a separate linked
  rebalancing work item** rather than silently re-worded.
- Tests cover the new model: a per-level deployment ends at its level's
  wave-10 clear, an early death is a loss, the report is deterministic for the
  same seeds/options, and the ring-1/ring-2 budget verdicts match the
  regenerated numbers.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries; the full
  project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Impact

A player's ring time is measured from the sortie they actually fly — one hex
level ending on its mini-boss — so the design doc's ring budgets describe real
play instead of the rest of the campaign.

## Constraints

- **Blocked by the mini-boss ending** (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2): tracked as a
  dependency edge. None of the epic's children are implemented and there are
  no mini-boss commits on `dev` at intake time, so a baseline regenerated
  before that behaviour ships would be re-run immediately.
- **The arena does not simulate a boss or mini-boss entity** (documented
  fidelity boundary in `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`): a mini-boss wave is its
  authored group composition. The measured sortie therefore ends when the
  wave-10 composition clears; the boss encounter's own duration is **not
  modelled**. Record that gap; modelling a mini-boss encounter is a linked
  follow-up, not scope here.
- **Per-level mode does not end on `level_cleared`**: `runArena` keeps ticking
  to `config.ticks` after the level clears, and `won` in non-campaign modes is
  `lives > 0 && aliveHostiles === 0` (a lingering asteroid keeps it false). The
  duration must therefore come from the `level_cleared` event, never from
  `ticksSimulated` or `won`.
- **Only the deployment model changes.** The aggression → level mapping
  (`hexDifficultyProfile`), the authored ring/hex data, the loadout resolution
  (`resolveDeploymentLoadout`, `ringEntryOwnership`), the retake chance
  (`DEFAULT_RETAKE_CHANCE_PERCENT`) and the 2-minute between-sortie allowance
  all stay as shipped, so the before/after delta is attributable.
- **Determinism is preserved**: the same seeds and options produce an identical
  report; the harness never reads the wall clock.
- **Numbers are never hand-edited** in `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` or
  the GDD table — the artifact is regenerated and the docs requote it.
- **Scope-creep clause.** Reporting per-deployment sortie length and sortie
  counts in the GDD table, modelling the mini-boss fight itself, re-authoring
  the 40–60 / 90–120 windows, and making the docs guard derive its means from
  the artifact (AH-0MW0KSCU20096B02) are **linked items**, not scope here. A
  ring whose budget no longer holds becomes its own linked rebalancing item.

## Existing state (researched, with evidence)

- **Deployment model as committed.** `createArenaDeploymentRunner`
  (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` ≈ line 767) runs `runArena` with `campaign:
  true` and `campaignLevels: campaignFromLevel(campaign, request.level)` — the
  campaign slice from the hex's level to the final boss. Duration is
  `result.ticksSimulated × request.dt`, capped by `RING_DEPLOYMENT_TICKS`
  (= `DEFAULT_BATCH_TICKS` = 18 000 ticks ≈ 300 s); `captured` is
  `result.won || ticksSimulated >= request.ticks`, i.e. "survived the window".
- **Retry model.** `DEFAULT_RETRY_MINUTES = RING_DEPLOYMENT_TICKS × dt / 60` =
  a flat **5 minutes** per loss, independent of what the run measured.
- **Committed baseline** (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, four
  ring/line reports, seeds 1–3, competent bot):

  | Ring | Line | Total mean (min–max) | Losses | Modelled deployment minutes | Budget |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 (6 hexes) | grind | 54.3 (51.0–56.6) | 4.7 | 19.0 | 40–60 · in-window |
  | 1 (6 hexes) | rush | 32.0 (31.9–32.2) | 1.0 | 0.5 | not-applicable |
  | 2 (12 hexes) | grind | 116.4 (112.7–123.4) | 10.7 | 39.1 | 90–120 · in-window |
  | 2 (12 hexes) | rush | 62.7 (60.9–63.6) | 0.7 | 3.4 | not-applicable |

  Roughly **3.2 minutes per deployment** on both grind lines, i.e. most of a
  deployment's time is the slice climbing campaign levels rather than the
  hex's own level — the quantity the one-level deployment removes.
- **Existing per-level seam.** `runArena` already supports an explicit `level`
  (per-level mode, AH-0MVLJFB1I0099X4Z) via `buildLevelWavePlan`, emitting
  `wave_cleared` / `level_cleared`; it is the closest shipped model of a
  one-level deployment.
- **Docs guards.** `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` pins the four means
  (`54.3`, `116.4`, `32.0`, `62.7`), the windows (40–60, 90–120), the tolerance
  (±2 min, ±3 min) and the artifact citation; `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`
  pins the literal windows and the real-arena budget assertions.

## Desired change

1. Play the shipped one-level deployment in the harness: the hex's
   aggression-selected level through the arena's per-level mode, measuring the
   `level_cleared` tick as the deployment's length.
2. Redefine the outcome model for one level: cleared level = captured,
   early death = loss, and a retry costs the replayed deployment's measured
   length (the 2-minute between-sortie allowance unchanged).
3. Regenerate `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` from the shipped code.
4. Reconcile GDD §8.2 and the docs guards with the regenerated numbers, and
   open a linked rebalancing item for every ring whose budget no longer holds.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` — the runner's deployment model (per-level mode,
  duration from `level_cleared`, captured/loss semantics, retry minutes from
  the measurement) and its module documentation.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — only if the `level_cleared` outcome needs a small,
  shared seam (read the emitted event; do not fork a second level-completion
  rule).
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — the one-level deployment model, outcome
  semantics, determinism and the regenerated budget verdicts.
- `scripts/ring-timing.mjs`, `scripts/ring-timing.test.ts` — CLI report/docs
  copy for the regenerate command.
- `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` — regenerated artifact (never
  hand-edited).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8.2 — measured table, playstyle numbers and
  the deployment-model sentence.
- `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` — the docs guard's means, windows and
  tolerance.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Expected (not a surprise): both rings may now miss their budgets.** The
  committed per-deployment time is ≈3.2 minutes, of which the slice climbing
  levels past the hex's own is most of it, so one-level sorties should shrink
  ring totals markedly — the item's own AC3 path (a linked rebalancing item per
  missed ring) is the likely outcome, not a defect in the new model.
- **Risk: the docs guard strands on literals.** `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`
  pins four hand-copied means, so a regeneration necessarily edits them by hand;
  AH-0MW0KSCU20096B02 is the structural fix (related, not blocking).
- **Risk: off-by-one level completion.** The `level_cleared` tick is emitted on
  the tick a wave-clear is detected, so the measured duration can be one tick
  long; pin the semantics in a test rather than leaving it to convention.
- **Risk: fidelity gap understates a real sortie.** The arena simulates no
  mini-boss entity, so the boss fight's duration is missing from the measured
  deployment; the brief records the gap and links a follow-up rather than
  inventing a constant.
- **Assumption: the aggression → level mapping, ring data, loadout model,
  retake chance and the 2-minute allowance stay shipped** (Q3 answer (a)), so
  the delta between the two baselines is attributable to the deployment model
  alone.
- **Assumption: the competent bot is the measurement line** (unchanged from the
  committed baseline), and seeds 1–3 remain the evidence set.

## Related work

- **In HexMap killing the mini-boss wins the hex (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2)** — the
  parent behaviour this measures; **blocking dependency** (`wl dep add`).
  Children of record: **Tests: hex deployment ends on its mini-boss
  (AH-0MWCOW3Z90015FJM)**, **Mini-boss victory captures the hex and ends the
  run (AH-0MWCOW4IQ003XST5)**, **Docs: the mini-boss ending and the win-path
  ordering (AH-0MWCOW7KO004D3EF)**.
- **Derive the ring-timing docs guard's measured means from the committed
  baseline artifact (AH-0MW0KSCU20096B02)** — would stop this regeneration from
  stranding the GDD guard on four hand-edited literals; related, not blocking.
- **Regenerate the ring-timing baseline evidence (AH-0MWB8VETE006YMVI)** —
  completed; regenerated the artifact under the *campaign-slice* model, so its
  numbers are superseded here, not its work.
- **Diagnose the competent bot's level-3 survival drift in the ring-timing
  arena (AH-0MWAPWS1W007LGGY)** — completed; documents the 5-minute-window
  survival boundary the current model relies on.
- **Ring timing validation and playstyle balance (AH-0MVUXCBQY001ESWT)** —
  completed; built the harness and pinned the 40–60 / 90–120 windows.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D — the design of record for the
  ring windows and the two playstyle lines.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — states the arena's documented level-3 survival/fire-model
  boundary the current measurements rest on.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MWB8VETE006YMVI** – Regenerate the ring-timing baseline evidence (completed)
- **AH-0MWBBU9QF000FXAP** – Conserving ring redistribution core (completed)
- **AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG** – Post-MVP Hangar War: hex variety (personalities, contracts, ring landmarks) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, aggression, artifact, assertion, baseline (+80 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: acceptance, aggression, artifact, assertion, baseline (+80 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: acceptance, artifact, baseline, becomes, boss (+77 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Sequencing** (this item measures behaviour that is not on `dev` yet).
  Options: (a) record a blocking dependency on the epic and park this item
  until the mini-boss ending lands; (b) build the per-level harness change now
  and re-run once the game change lands; (c) fold the measurement into the
  mini-boss epic as a final child. **Recommended:** (a).
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (a).** Action taken:
  `wl dep add AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2`.
- **Q2 — What "deployment duration" means now.** Options: (a) end the measured
  deployment at the arena's `level_cleared` tick (the wave-10 mini-boss kill),
  charging a loss for dying before it; (b) keep charging the fixed 5-minute
  window. **Recommended:** (a) — otherwise the 300 s window keeps dominating
  and nothing moves.
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (a).**
- **Q3 — Between-sortie allowance.** Options: (a) keep the flat 2 minutes,
  unchanged and still documented, so the only moving input is the deployment
  model; (b) re-time it from the shipped UI in this item.
  **Recommended:** (a). **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (a).**
- **Settled without asking** — AC3's rule that a ring whose budget no longer
  holds becomes a separate linked item (rather than re-worded) was taken as
  decided by the item's own acceptance criteria; the 5-minute retry assumption
  becomes the replayed deployment's measured length, which follows mechanically
  from Q2(a).
- **Research note** — the arena has no boss/mini-boss entity (documented
  fidelity boundary, `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` § module doc), so a one-level
  measurement ends at the wave-10 composition clear; the mini-boss fight's own
  duration is unmodelled and is recorded as a known gap and a linked
  follow-up.
- **Q4 — What does the rush line's re-capture allowance charge now?** Asked by
  plan, 2026-11-11, because the exposure allowance charges
  `expectedRetakes × (deployment + visit)` and the only "deployment" price it
  has is the retired 18 000-tick window (5 min) — 53.9 of the 62.7 measured
  ring-2 rush minutes. Options: (a) charge a re-capture the line's **measured
  mean deployment** + the 2-minute visit; (b) keep the documented 18 000-tick
  window, so the before/after delta stays attributable to the retry change
  alone; (c) land (a) with (b) reported as a sensitivity figure.
  **Recommended: (a)** — leaving a fixed 5-minute *deployment* price in the
  model after removing the 5-minute deployment window would make the harness
  price a deployment two different ways.
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-11-11): (a).** Carried into the
  plan as: the re-capture allowance charges the line's measured mean deployment
  + the unchanged 2-minute between-sortie visit, pinned by a test.
- **Q5 — May this item proceed even though the mini-boss epic is not yet terminal?**
  Asked by implement, 2026-11-12, because every implementation child of the epic
  (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2) is already committed on `dev`, but the epic itself stays
  `in-progress` while only its docs child (AH-0MWCOW7KO004D3EF) is open, so
  `implement.py drive` fails closed on the non-terminal dependency edge. Options:
  (a) treat the block as satisfied/stale and start the chain now; (b) keep the
  formal gate — wait until the epic reaches `in_review`, then re-run unchanged.
  **Recommended: (a).** **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-11-12): (b).**
  The dependency edge stays; the item is re-dispatched when the epic lands.
  Recorded in comment AH-C0MWDEHPQ0002QCPJ.

## Plan (plan_complete, 2026-11-11)

Effort/risk pre-check: `decision: plan` (Small / Medium). Plan-approval gate:
`request_approval: false` (the gate requests approval only for Extra Large
effort **and** High/Severe risk), so no approval pause was taken.

### Features (test-first, in dependency order)

1. **Tests: one-level deployment semantics (AH-0MWCQ4EZD006YWHV)** — red-first
   tests pin the new model before any production change: duration = the
   `level_cleared` tick × `dt`, death-before-clear is a loss, duration never
   read from `ticksSimulated`/`won`, retry = the replayed deployment's measured
   length, the 2-minute between-sortie allowance unchanged, re-capture = the
   line's measured mean + visit (Q4 = a), determinism. *Blocked by the
   mini-boss ending epic (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2).*
2. **Implement: harness plays the one-level deployment (AH-0MWCQ4FWN009J9DM)** —
   `createArenaDeploymentRunner` switches to the arena's per-level mode at the
   hex's aggression-selected level, derives duration/outcome from the emitted
   `level_cleared` event, derives retry minutes from the measurement, updates
   the re-capture basis, and rewrites the module documentation. *Blocked by 1.*
3. **Regenerate the ring-timing baseline artifact (AH-0MWCQ4GTE005YG02)** —
   `npm run ring-timing -- --json --out docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` on
   the shipped code, two runs byte-identical, before/after split recorded, no
   hand-edited numbers. *Blocked by 2.*
4. **Budget verdicts and linked rebalancing items (AH-0MWCQ4HTC004U73V)** —
   judge each ring's grind total against its authored window, pin the verdicts
   in tests, and open one linked rebalancing item per ring whose budget no
   longer holds (measurement, delta, split, options). Windows are **not**
   re-authored here. *Blocked by 3.*
5. **Docs and guards requote the regenerated numbers (AH-0MWCQ4IS6001X7W3)** —
   GDD §8.2 (measured table, playstyle figures, the "a deployment is" sentence),
   `docs/EVALUATION.md`, `README.md`, and the guards
   (`src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`, `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts`)
   requote the artifact; a missed ring is stated as `missed` with its linked
   rebalancing item. *Blocked by 4.*

### Model of record after this item

- **A deployment** is the hex's aggression-selected level, played through the
  arena's per-level mode to its wave-10 composition clear; its length is the
  `level_cleared` tick × `dt`.
- **Outcome** — cleared level = captured; a death before it = loss.
- **Retry** — a loss is charged the replayed deployment's **measured** length
  (no flat 5-minute window).
- **Between sorties** — 2 minutes, unchanged.
- **Re-capture (rush)** — the line's measured mean deployment + the 2-minute
  visit at the shipped 70 % frontier attack chance (Q4 = a).
- **Unchanged by design** — the aggression → level mapping, the authored ring
  data, `resolveDeploymentLoadout`/`ringEntryOwnership`, the retake chance, the
  2-minute allowance and the authored ring windows, so the before/after delta is
  attributable to the deployment model.

### Phasing (vertical slices)

Five phases, each cutting through the layers it owns (code, tests, docs) and
each one ending in a committable, reviewed slice: tests → harness model →
regenerated evidence → verdicts/links → documents and guards. Between phases,
re-read the next item and update its description with the numbers the previous
phase measured (especially item 4's verdicts before item 5 writes prose).

### Deliberately out of scope

Reporting per-deployment sortie length and sortie counts in the GDD table,
modelling the mini-boss encounter itself, re-authoring the 40–60 / 90–120
windows, and deriving the docs guard's means from the artifact
(AH-0MW0KSCU20096B02) — all linked items, not this plan. A ring whose budget no
longer holds becomes its own linked rebalancing item (item 4).

### Risks carried into the plan

- **Docs guards strand on literals** — item 5 edits four hand-copied means by
  hand; AH-0MW0KSCU20096B02 is the structural fix, not a blocker.
- **Off-by-one level completion** — the `level_cleared` event fires on the tick
  a wave-clear is detected and the loop keeps ticking past it; item 1 pins the
  tick convention literally, item 2 must never read `ticksSimulated`/`won`.
- **Run cost past the clear** — a cleared level is still simulated to
  `config.ticks`; if that makes regeneration impractical, item 2 records the
  cost and files a follow-up rather than changing arena semantics.
- **Fidelity gap** — the arena simulates no mini-boss entity, so the measured
  sortie ends at the wave-10 composition clear; every document restating the
  model must say so (item 5).
- **Both rings may miss their windows** — expected, not a defect; item 4 turns
  each miss into a linked rebalancing item rather than a re-worded budget.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-11 — plan session: recorded Q4 (producer answer (a)); created 5 child
  items with test-first dependency edges (`AH-0MWCQ4EZD006YWHV` →
  `AH-0MWCQ4FWN009J9DM` → `AH-0MWCQ4GTE005YG02` → `AH-0MWCQ4HTC004U73V` →
  `AH-0MWCQ4IS6001X7W3`), the first blocked by the mini-boss epic; ran the six
  review stages and the acceptance-criteria coverage review; stage advanced to
  `plan_complete`.


- 2026-11-13 — plan re-run (herdr-downtime dispatch): re-validated the plan
  after the mini-boss epic reached terminal state. The formal gate is now
  satisfied: In HexMap killing the mini-boss wins the hex
  (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2) is `completed`/`done` and its docs child

  `recommendation: proceed`; approval gate: `request_approval: false`. No
  children created or changed (idempotent re-run); stage re-advanced to
  `plan_complete`.

# Re-baseline salvage, cores and the mini-boss reward value per hex deployment (AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA)

## Producer decision (2026-11-13, recorded)

**Q1 = (c)** — On a winning hex deployment, the mini-boss wheel is **suppressed**
and the player instead **banks a fixed post-win bonus** into the hangar war
(answer to the OPEN QUESTION inherited from AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2). The wheel
stays as shipped on every other path (the arcade campaign and lost hangar
deployments). The fixed bonus **amount** is a balance knob; it is set in the
linked economy-rule item (either producer-specified or baselined from this
item's measured per-deployment income).

## Problem statement

The mini-boss ending (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2) turned a hex deployment from a
campaign slice (the hex's aggression-selected level through to the campaign's
final boss, banking salvage at every level's mini-boss) into **one** campaign
level ending on its wave-10 mini-boss. The measured economy therefore changes:
a deployment now banks salvage at exactly **one** checkpoint moment (one mini-
boss, one core) instead of several, per-deployment income drops, and the
unlock pace for rings 1–2 moves. Separately, that same ending presents the
mini-boss wheel reward **after the run has already finished** (producer
ordering Q2 = b), so the wheel's run-scoped permanent upgrades are spent on a
completed run — an open design question no measurement alone can answer.

## Users

- **As a Hangar War player**, I want the salvage and cores I bank per hex
  deployment to be measured against the sorties I actually fly (one level, one
  mini-boss), so the design doc's economy figures describe real play and the
  unlock tree prices make sense against real income.
- **As a Hangar War player**, I want a winning deployment's mini-boss reward
  to be worth something I can see, so a post-win wheel does not read as a
  broken reward that disappears into a finished run.
- **As a producer**, I want a measured before/after of per-deployment
  salvage/cores and the rings-1–2 unlock pace, plus a recorded ruling on the
  post-win reward's value, so any rebalancing rests on evidence and a named
  decision rather than estimates.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Per-deployment salvage/cores measured on the shipped one-level
   deployment.** The measured report states, for the shipped one-level
   deployment (the hex's aggression-selected level through its wave-10
   mini-boss), the salvage banked per deployment — **minerals** held at the
   single mini-boss checkpoint and **cores** (one per captured deployment) —
   for rings 1 and 2 and both playstyle lines, and compares them with the
   pre-change figures (the committed campaign-slice artifact's banked-salvage
   lines and the GDD §8.2 economy notes). The measurement is reproducible
   (same seeds/options → same numbers) and the numbers are never hand-edited.
2. **Unlock pace for rings 1–2.** The report derives, from the measured
   per-deployment income, the reachable-unlock pace for the rings-1–2
   catalogue entries (deployments needed to afford each entry, using the
   shipped prices in `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`), shown as a before/after
   table so a balance verdict is possible at a glance.
3. **Producer decision recorded.** The OPEN QUESTION about a post-win mini-boss
   reward is answered by the producer (2026-11-13): **suppress the wheel on the
   win path and bank a fixed post-win bonus** — recorded explicitly on this
   work item (Appendix Q1). The bonus amount is a balance knob owned by the
   linked economy-rule item, not a number this item must invent.
4. **Any balance change is a linked item.** The implementation of the producer's
   decision — suppressing the wheel on the win path and banking the fixed

   `related-to:<this-id>`), never folded in here. A further verdict that the
   measured income/unlock pace implies a price, banking or ring change is also
   filed as its own linked item.
5. **Documentation and tests.** The GDD §8.2 economy notes (and any affected
   code comments) are updated to quote the new measured figures with the
   before/after comparison, the reward-value decision and the linked items;
   code comments that describe the banking model state the measured facts;

A player's banked income and unlock pace are measured from the shorter sortie
they actually fly, and the post-win mini-boss reward has a named, recorded

designed once a hex is a bite-sized sortie.

  and links — a change to banking, prices, the wheel's win-path application or
  windows is a separate item (AC4). The reward-value *ruling* (Q1 = c) is
  recorded here; the *implementation* — suppressing the wheel on the win path
  and banking the fixed bonus — is the linked economy-rule item.
- **After-income includes the bonus once its amount is set.** The measured
  per-deployment income is reported first without the bonus, then with the
  fixed bonus overlaid once the linked item's amount is fixed, so the report
  is comparable across the decision either way.

  committed campaign-slice artifact (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`,
  its `banked salvage` summary lines) and the GDD §8.2 economy notes; the
  campaign-slice harness model is not re-run for a synthetic before. The
  artifact's cores are derived from the documented checkpoint-banking model
  (one mini-boss defeat per checkpoint bank; a campaign slice defeated several
  mini-bosses per captured deployment), stated as a model estimate where not
  directly measured.
- **One-level deployment is shipped.** Measurement targets the shipped
  behaviour of AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2 (on `dev`); no re-architecting of the
  banking rule, the wheel or the harness's arena.
- **Harness sharing with the ring-timing re-baseline.** The headless
  ring-timing harness is the measurement seam; AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A plans the
  same runner's one-level rework. This item reuses that seam when landed, or
  builds the income reporting (minerals + cores) on the shipped runner
  deterministically — whichever ships first — and the two items share the
  numbers rather than forking a second harness (see Related work).
- **Cores must be modelled explicitly.** The harness counts minerals via
  telemetry but models no checkpoint cores today; a one-level deployment's
  cores equal its captured count (one mini-boss per deployment), so the report
  adds the core view without inventing a new banking rule.

# Tests: one-level deployment semantics (AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A child 1)

**Test-first item.** Pin the *new* deployment semantics in tests **before** any
production change lands, so the harness change in the sibling item is driven by
a failing specification rather than by convention.

Parent: Re-measure ring timing for one-level hex deployments
(AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A). Blocked by **In HexMap killing the mini-boss wins the
hex (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2)**: the behaviour under measurement does not exist on
`dev` yet, so this item is parked rather than closed.

## Context

`createArenaDeploymentRunner` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) currently plays the
**classic campaign slice** (`campaign: true`, `campaignLevels:
campaignFromLevel(campaign, request.level)`) and derives a deployment's length
from `result.ticksSimulated × dt`, with `captured = result.won ||
result.ticksSimulated >= request.ticks` — i.e. "survived the 300 s window".
That model no longer describes the game: a deployment is one hex, one level,
ending on that level's wave-10 mini-boss.

The arena **already** supports the seam this needs: per-level mode
(`runArena({ level })`, `buildLevelWavePlan`) emits `level_cleared` on the tick
the final wave is detected clear (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, per-level wave gate),
and the event record carries `tick`. Per-level mode keeps ticking after the
level clears and its `won` is `lives > 0 && aliveHostiles === 0` (a lingering
asteroid keeps it false), so **neither `ticksSimulated` nor `won` may be used**
for the deployment's duration or outcome.

## Scope (tests only — no production edit)

Add a `describe('ring timing: the one-level deployment model')` block to
`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` that fails until the sibling implementation
item lands, pinning:

- **Duration** — a deployment's length is the tick of its level's
  `level_cleared` event × `dt`; the one-tick emission convention is pinned
  literally so a later refactor cannot silently shift every deployment.
- **Outcome** — a run that reaches `level_cleared` is **captured**; a
  `player_death` before it is a **loss**, charged its own measured length.
- **Not-from-the-run-fields** — a case where the level clears but the run keeps
  ticking to `config.ticks` (and `won` is false because an asteroid lingers)
  still measures the clear tick, not the run length.
- **Retry price** — a lost deployment's retry charge is the replayed
  deployment's own measured length × `retriesPerLoss`; the flat
  `DEFAULT_RETRY_MINUTES` (300 s) is no longer the retry price.
- **Between-sortie allowance** — still a flat, documented **2 minutes**,
  pinned literally.
- **Re-capture price (Q1 = a)** — the rush line's exposure allowance charges a
  re-capture the line's measured mean deployment **+ the 2-minute visit**,
  not the retired 18 000-tick window.
- **Determinism** — the same seeds and options produce an identical report
  (deployment seconds, retry minutes, re-capture minutes and totals).

Use an injected fake runner (`RingTimingOptions.runDeployment`) for the model
semantics and one small real-arena case for the `level_cleared` seam. Keep the
new block under 30 s of wall time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` contains a one-level-deployment test block whose cases cover duration, captured/loss, the not-from-`ticksSimulated`/`won` guard, retry price, the 2-minute between-sortie allowance, the re-capture price and determinism.
- Every new case fails on the pre-change harness (red-first evidence recorded in a comment: the assertion messages, not a pasted log) and names the parent work item in the block's doc comment.
- No production file is modified by this item (`git show --stat` shows only the test file).
- The test block runs in under 30 s and introduces no new test-time random source.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- The full project test suite passes once the sibling implementation item has landed (expected to be red on this item alone, which is recorded in the item's completion comment).

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — the new one-level-deployment test block (the only file this item edits).
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` — read-only reference: the current campaign-slice runner and the model inputs the tests pin.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — read-only reference: the per-level wave gate that emits `level_cleared` with its tick.

# Implement: harness plays the one-level deployment (AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A child 2)

Parent: Re-measure ring timing for one-level hex deployments
(AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A). Prerequisite: **Tests: one-level deployment semantics**.

## Context

The committed baseline (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`) models a
deployment as the campaign **slice** from the hex's aggression-selected level to
the campaign's final boss. The mini-boss ending (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2) turns a
deployment into exactly one campaign level, ending on that level's wave-10
mini-boss, so every measured number and every derived ring window moves. This
item changes the model; it does **not** change the aggression mapping
(`hexDifficultyProfile`), the authored ring data, the loadout resolution, the
retake chance or the 2-minute between-sortie allowance.

## Desired change

1. `createArenaDeploymentRunner` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) plays the
   **shipped one-level deployment**: `runArena` in per-level mode at
   `request.level` (the hex's aggression-selected level), keeping the launch
   `startingLoadout`, the seeded balance config and the existing tick cap as the
   run's safety bound.
2. The deployment's **duration** comes from the arena's `level_cleared` event
   tick (`× dt`) — never from `ticksSimulated` and never from `won`, both of
   which describe the tick loop rather than the level.
3. The **outcome** is `captured` when `level_cleared` was observed and `loss`
   when the player died before it.
4. The **retry allowance** charges the replayed deployment's own measured
   length (`measuredMinutes × retriesPerLoss`) instead of the flat
   `DEFAULT_RETRY_MINUTES` (300 s). `DEFAULT_RETRY_MINUTES` must no longer be
   the retry price; either delete it or redefine it as an explicitly documented
   fallback/sensitivity knob with no default use.
5. The **re-capture allowance** (rush line) charges a re-capture the line's
   measured mean deployment + the 2-minute visit, replacing the retired
   18 000-tick window (producer ruling Q1 = a on the parent item).
6. The module documentation and code comments state the new model end to end
   (`## What is measured, what is modelled` and `## Fidelity boundary`): one
   level, ending on the wave-10 composition clear; the mini-boss encounter's own
   duration is **not** modelled; retries cost the measured replay; re-captures
   cost the measured mean + visit.

**Do not** fork a second level-completion rule or change arena semantics: read
the emitted event. If simulating past the clear makes the regeneration
impractically slow, record the measured wall-clock cost and file a follow-up
item rather than changing `runArena` in this item.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `createArenaDeploymentRunner` runs the arena in per-level mode at `request.level` and derives each deployment's `seconds` from the `level_cleared` event tick; no path reads `ticksSimulated` or `won` for a deployment's duration or outcome.

- The rush line's re-capture allowance charges the line's measured mean deployment + the documented 2-minute between-sortie visit; the 2-minute allowance itself is unchanged.

- The module documentation states the one-level deployment, the measured `level_cleared` duration, the measured replay cost, the measured-mean re-capture cost and the unmodelled mini-boss encounter.
- No arena semantic change: `git show --stat` touches no other module's behaviour, or, if a shared seam proves unavoidable, the change is minimal, documented and covered by an arena test.

# Defense report should be rolled into the hex map screen

## Problem statement

The between-sortie defence report is a separate textual screen (`DefenceReportScene`) that the player must click through after every deployment, even though the hex map already knows every hex and its attack history. The report's information — which hexes were attacked, whether they held or fell, and the numbers behind it — belongs on the map itself, so the player sees the outcomes spatially, in the context of the ring, without an intermediate screen.

## Users

- **Hangar War player (primary):** after a deployment ends, wants to see at a glance where attacks occurred on the ring, and to inspect the numbers behind a specific attack by focusing the hex(es) involved — without a separate report screen.
  - *User story:* "When my deployment ends I land back on the hex map and see arrows showing where the frontier attacked. I move focus to the hex that fell and read on the left exactly what happened — attacking force, aggression, defender rating, margin — and what I need to do about it."
- **Attract-mode watcher:** the demo must never stall on (or have to click through) a removed screen; the map's arrows render from the same transient record and the demo continues exactly as it did from the report.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Flow: deployment ends on the hex map.** After a Hangar War deployment finishes, `PlayScene` starts `HexMapScene` directly (not `DefenceReportScene`), passing the tick record, the run result line (VICTORY/DEFEAT · score) and any won mini-boss reward; `DefenceReportScene` is removed from the shipped scene list and module surface (`src/core/gameConfig.ts`, `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts`), and a test drives the win path with no `DefenceReportScene` in the game config.
- **Attack arrows.** The hex map renders one arrow per attack in the most recent between-sortie tick record, from the attacker-origin hex to the attacked hex, positioned from the record's axial coordinates on the existing `axialToPixel` layout; the arrow data derives from a shared pure model (no per-scene rule), and a test asserts an arrow exists for every `record.attacks` entry and points at the correct target hex.
- **Left-hand attack-details panel.** When the focused hex is either endpoint of an attack arrow (the attacked hex OR its attacker-origin hex), a new panel on the LEFT of the map shows that attack's details (the numbers the resolved tick recorded — outcome, attacking force, aggression, defender rating, attack strength, margin, retake plan); the existing right-hand intel panel stays untouched; when the focused hex is not involved in any attack, the left panel hides. Tests pin the panel text for both endpoint kinds and its absence for an uninvolved hex.
- **Transient arrows, no persistence.** The arrows and attack panels reflect only the most recent between-sortie tick record carried from the deployment and are cleared when the map is re-entered without a record (e.g. from the menu/hangar later); no new payload field or store migration is introduced and no attack history is persisted.
- **Win-path reward still presents, over the paused map.** The mini-boss reward a winning deployment resolves is presented via the shipped `MiniBossWheelScene`/`MineralChoiceScene` overlay with the map paused, then the map resumes normal interaction; the existing win-path ordering test (reward → map interaction) is kept green by moving it onto the map.
- **Gym↔game parity maintained.** `GymHexWar` renders the same integrated map renderer (arrows + left attack panel) when given the same record, and its report view/`DEFENCE_REPORT` seam is updated or removed consistently; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` is updated to reflect the rolled-in report. The changed-scope test gate passes and the full suite stays green.
- **All related documentation updated.** Code comments, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D section, GDD §8.2 (defence report), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` and any README/wiki entries describing the between-sortie report screen reflect the rolled-in design, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Impact

Players no longer click through a separate textual report screen — after a deployment they land on the hex map where arrows show where the frontier attacked and the left panel explains the numbers behind any attack they focus.

## Constraints

- **View only, no re-derivation:** the arrows and attack panel copy every number from the tick record (via the shared `buildDefenceReport` model); no scene may recompute an attack, an outcome or a margin (gym↔game parity, AGENTS.md).
- **No store change:** nothing new is persisted; attacker-origin coordinates already travel in `FrontierTickRecord.attacks[]` (`attackerOrigin` + `hexId`), so arrows render from existing launch-data (transient, Q2 = a).
- **Parity surface:** the map renderer (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`) and its read model are shared with `GymHexWar`; any change must land there once (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).
- Pure models keep no Phaser imports in `src/core/hangarWar/`; UK English in UI strings.
- The shared `FocusManager` drives focus; the left panel keys off the focused row like the right panel does today.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._finishRun` → `this.scene.start(DEFENCE_REPORT_SCENE_KEY, { payload, record, won, score, reward, demo, demoDwellMs })` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:5601` region).
- `DefenceReportScene` renders `buildDefenceReport(payload, record)` via `renderDefenceReport` and has one action (continue → map); win-path reward is presented over the paused report, then `_startMap()`.
- `HexMapScene` currently accepts `{ payload, storage, definitions, demo, demoDwellMs }` only — no record, no run line, no reward.
- `renderHexMap` already draws tiles via `axialToPixel(intel.q, intel.r)` and has a right-hand detail panel keyed to the focused hex (`PANEL_X = GAME_WIDTH - 260`); the left area (x ≈ 24) currently holds header lines and the HANGAR row.
- `FrontierTickRecord` carries `attacks[]`, each with `hexId`, `attackerOriginId`, `attackerOrigin { q, r }` and the full `DefenceResolution` numbers — everything an arrow and a details panel need.
- Gym: `GymHexWar` renders `renderHexMap` (map view) and `renderDefenceReport` (report view) with no handlers; parity pinned in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
- Demo traversal: `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` includes a `defenceReport` screen decision (`continueToMap`), driven by `decideReportAction`; `hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts` walks menu → hangar → map → deployment → report → map and pins win-path ordering (report → reward → map).

## Desired change

- `HexMapSceneData` gains `record?: FrontierTickRecord`, `won?: boolean | null`, `score?: number`, `reward?: MiniBossWinReward | null`; `PlayScene._finishRun` starts `HEX_MAP_SCENE_KEY` with these instead of the report scene.
- `buildHexMapModel` (or a sibling pure helper over the tick record) exposes the attack arrows (origin id/coords → target id) and the per-attack details keyed by hex id; `renderHexMap` draws arrows on the axial grid and adds a left-hand details panel that shows the attack block when the focused hex is an arrow endpoint, hiding otherwise.
- Win-path reward presentation moves from `DefenceReportScene` onto a paused `HexMapScene` (same overlay launch/resume contract); demo mode auto-resolves it as today.
- `DefenceReportScene` and its registration are deleted; `decideReportAction`/the `defenceReport` traversal screen are removed from `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` and its tests (the map decision already never stalls).
- `GymHexWar` swaps its report view for the integrated map+arrows view (or drops the seam), and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` is updated.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_finishRun` deployment branch starts `HexMapScene` with record/run-line/reward instead of `DefenceReportScene`.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — new launch-data fields; reward-over-paused-map presentation; passes record into the shared renderer.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — draws attack arrows (origin → target via `axialToPixel`) and the left-hand attack-details panel.
- `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` + `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — the shared pure model(s) exposing arrow + per-attack detail data from the record (kept Phaser-free).
- `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts` / `src/scenes/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` — removed (or repurposed); `src/core/gameConfig.ts` scene list updated.
- `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` (+ tests) — drop the `defenceReport` screen decision.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` + `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — gym renders the integrated map view.
- Tests: `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/hangarWar/defenceReport.test.ts`, `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP** — Between-sortie defence report and attract-mode traversal (completed; the scene this item replaces).
- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** — Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed; the map surface being extended).
- **AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2** — In HexMap killing the mini-boss wins the hex (completed; parent of the win-path reward flow this item relocates).
- **AH-0MWCOW61X002LL10** — Tests: win-path ordering report then reward then map (completed; ordering test moves onto the map).
- **AH-0MWBBUAUQ0038GFL** — Defence report and intel render redistribution (completed; related report view-model work).
- **AH-0MWDBI33V003QQ3U** — Hangar Map UX (open; separate map-layout item — watch for left-panel layout overlap).
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** — Text on hex map is unreadable (completed; the readability bar the new left panel must meet).
- Docs: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D, GDD §8.2 "The defence report", `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MWDBI33V003QQ3U** – Hangar Map UX (open)
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** – Text on hex map is unreadable (completed)
- **AH-0MUE86S5F002VVQD** – Leaderboard entry screen should show position in table (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `README.md` — matches the item's keywords (add/arrows/attack/…); check for claimed report-screen behaviour to update.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — contains the "defence report" (§8.2) and hex-map sections this item rewrites.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — keyword hits only, not directly affected.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — left/right panel overlap:** `AH-0MWDBI33V003QQ3U` (Hangar Map UX, open) may also move map UI around; the new left panel must not collide with the header/HANGAR rows on the left edge or the right intel panel when both land. Mitigation: place the attack panel in a dedicated left band and note the coordinate choice in the item; conflict is coordination-only (no shared file rule).
- **Risk — reward regression:** moving `_presentReward`/`_afterReward` from the report scene onto the map risks the "reward never shown" or "map unresponsive" failure modes; the shipped win-path test (`hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts`) pins ordering and provides the red/green gate.
- **Risk — demo stall:** removing the report screen removes a traversal hop; the bot must continue straight from map → deploy → map, so `decideReportAction` removal must not leave a screen without a decision. Mitigation: the map decision (`decideMapAction`) is already total; traversal tests cover it.
- **Assumption — transient record:** arrows/panels reflect only the carried tick record and vanish on later map re-entry (Q2 = a); run result line and reward are carried once, like today.
- **Assumption — quiet tick:** a tick with no attacks draws no arrows and the left panel stays hidden (no new empty-state copy needed).
- **Scope-creep guard:** attack *history*, arrow styling/fancy VFX, and persistent per-attack storage are deliberately out of scope (Q2 = a); record them as separate work items rather than expanding this change.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Fate of `DefenceReportScene` and the win-path reward — (a) remove the scene, a deployment ends straight on the map carrying record + run line + reward, reward overlay over the paused map (recommended); (b) keep it as an optional deeper report behind a key; (c) repurpose into a transient report banner on the map." — Answer (producer): **a**. Source: producer reply 2026-11-13.
- Q2: "Arrow scope and persistence — (a) only the most recent between-sortie tick's attacks, transient, cleared when the map is re-entered later, no store migration (recommended); (b) persist attack history in the payload." — Answer (producer): **a**. Source: producer reply 2026-11-13.
- Q3: "Left panel semantics and 'hexes involved' — (a) new LEFT attack-details panel when the focused hex is either arrow endpoint, right-hand intel panel stays, hides when not involved (recommended); (b) replace the right-hand panel; (c) only the attacked target shows details." — Answer (producer): **a**. Source: producer reply 2026-11-13.

As a player, I want hulls to be able to grant **extra upgrade bays** (more equipment/loadout slots than the base hull) as a special-reward axis, so the special-mission reward space is not limited to more hit points.

Follow-on from the producer's answer to Q2 on **AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55** ("2. A — create a work item to add upgrade bays"): the special-missions item ships its first reward as a hull with extra hit points; the **upgrade-bay concept does not yet exist in the data model** (HullRunStats carries only startingLives + speedMultiplier; upgrades are armour/firepower/systems), so extending the run-stats/loadout model for upgrade bays is tracked separately here.

Part of the Hangar War's **post-MVP mitigation backlog** (discovered-from:AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55, recorded in `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D and GDD §8.2).

## Scope

- Introduce an **upgrade-bay concept** to the hangar hull model: a hull authoring how many bays (equipment/loadout slots) it deploys with, resolved into the run loadout and persisted under the existing `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload.
- Futures a hull reward that grants **extra upgrade bays** rather than (or in addition to) extra hit points — the second special reward the design of record names.

# Feature: Seeded rotation resolver for special-mission offers

## Goal
Implement a pure, seeded resolver that selects which special-mission hex (and its reward) is offered between sorties. The resolver is a pure function of the payload `seed` via the shared `createHangarWarRng` stream — deterministic and replayable, no scene-level randomness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — A new resolver function (in `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` or a small module beside `fakeFrontierClock.ts`) selects one special-mission hex from the ring based on a per-sortie derived seed (mixed from the payload `seed` and the current sortie index).
- **AC2** — The resolver is a pure function — given the same payload `seed` and sortie index, it always returns the same hex index.
- **AC3** — The resolver is integrated into the ring deployment/payload lifecycle: it is called once at sortie start, the chosen hex is stored in the payload (or derived deterministically each sortie from the stored seed + sortie counter), and it respects already-captured hexes (skipping secured hexes).
- **AC4** — The resolver is consumed by `buildHexMapModel` / `hexIntel` so that the chosen offer is published in the known-ahead intel surface.
- **AC5 (traces to parent AC3)** — The presented special hex/offer rotates between sorties from the shared seeded RNG and is deterministic for the payload seed, so the same seed yields the same rotation sequence with never ad-hoc randomness in a scene.

## Key Files

- `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` (or a small new module beside the frontier-clock module)
- `src/core/hangarWar/fakeFrontierClock.ts` (per-tick stream model to follow as a pattern reference)
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` (payload/hex state) / `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` (store) — only if the chosen hex is stored in the payload

## Constraints

- Derived from the payload `seed` via `createHangarWarRng` — never ad-hoc randomness in a scene.
- Deterministic and replayable for a given seed; rotation must stay legible (published known-ahead).

## Risky assumptions

- Exact rotation stream derivation (per-sortie vs per-tick mix) is a design detail; follow the `fakeFrontierClock.ts` tickSeed model.

## Deliverables

- New or extended module in `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` with the rotation resolver.
- Integration of the resolver into the ring deployment and intel model.
